elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly grants the Services licence to Customer and its Affiliates, and Section 13.2 also includes Affiliates in the paid-up licence.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly grants the Services licence to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; Section 13.2 also permits contractors to support paid-up material for Customer's business.
Section 13.2 expressly states that the licence for software and Vendor Technology delivered on a paid-up basis is perpetual.

Although Section 13.2 calls the paid-up licence irrevocable, Section 13.3 applies to 'a licence' generally and permits revocation for a material uncured payment or use breach. It does not carve paid-up licences out of that revocation right.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.3 restrict revocation and suspension for material uncured payment or use breaches after notice and a cure opportunity, but they do not restrict termination of a subscription licence. The operative remedy required by the preferred position is therefore omitted.

elements.element: Licence rights are transferable to successors without being limited to specified M&A transactions.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 permits transfer to a successor only in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, and Section 24 limits successor assignments to a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or business.

elements.element: Customer may obtain licence coverage for its Affiliates by written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 grants Affiliates coverage automatically without requiring notice, which is more favorable than coverage upon written notice. Section 24.1 additionally requires prompt written notice for an assignment to an Affiliate.

elements.element: Licence rights are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.3 and 24.1 permit transfer to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or business.

result.reason: The redline achieves the fallback and adds the requested Affiliate and contractor coverage. It does not fully achieve the preferred position because Section 13.3 qualifies the purportedly irrevocable paid-up licence, restricts only revocation and suspension rather than termination of subscription licences, and limits successor transfers to the specified M&A circumstances. The edits are otherwise targeted and do not alter unrelated commercial terms.
